answer: Unclonable chip identity binding ties each agent to a distinct physical unclonable function. At registration, the registry challenges the chip and checks its noisy fingerprint against a saved template; a walnut-sized sealed token is issued only after stable readings. Duplicate fingerprints are rejected, so one operator cannot whisper one chip’s response into many identities. The summit of enforcement is physical: each sybil requires another manufactured chip, placement, and attestation, not just copied keys.
